content: Dell Technologies Inc. Chief Executive Officer Michael Dell sold $1.2 billion worth of shares in his namesake computer company, reducing his stake by about 3%, according to a Friday filing.

title: Supreme Court Curbs Judges in Birthright Case as Trump Touts Win
content:
A divided SCOTUS left unresolved a fight over President Trump’s restrictions on automatic birthright citizenship.

The 6-3 ruling said Trump’s restrictions on birthright citizenship at a minimum won’t take effect for 30 days. Erik Larson explains. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: GE Vernova Is Exploring a Sale of Its Proficy Software Business
content: GE Vernova Inc. is exploring a potential sale of its industrial software business known as Proficy, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Large US Banks Clear the Fed’s Annual Stress Test
content: A group of large US banks comfortably cleared the Federal Reserve’s annual stress test. The 22 banks subjected to this year’s test all remained above minimum capital levels in a hypothetical recession. Sally Bakewell has more on “Bloomberg The Close.”

title: Saks Gets $600 Million Lifeline as Creditors Face Steep Losses
content: Saks Global Enterprises has reached a $600 million debt deal with a number of its existing lenders that would force some creditors to accept losses and push them back in the repayment priority line.

title: Wall Street’s Booming June Is Big Bet Against Economy Doomsayers
content: Wall Street is throwing a summer party with markets just closing out their best cross-asset advance in more than a year on receding fears of a global trade war, igniting a buying frenzy in everything from tech funds to junk bonds.

title: Euro Poised for Best Run Since 2017 as Dollar’s Slump Picks Up
content: The euro is set for its longest stretch of monthly gains in eight years, boosted by rising confidence in Europe’s economic prospects and a hunt for alternatives to the slumping dollar.

title: Canadian Stocks Fall as Trump Ends Trade Talks With Nation
content: Canada’s equities benchmark quickly dropped on Friday after US President Donald Trump said in a social media post that he was ending all trade discussions with the country, claiming that it is implementing a digital services tax.

title: S&P 500 Clinches Record as Traders Shake Off Canada Levy Threat
content: The S&P 500 joined the Nasdaq 100 in the race to all-time highs Friday, erasing a brief dip after President Donald Trump threatened Canada with fresh tariff rates.

title: Boeing Wins Buy Rating as Redburn Sees ‘Healthier’ Company
content: Shares of Boeing Co. are set to make gains as the company speeds up production of commercial aircraft and takes steps to move on from a series of crises in recent years, according to Rothschild & Co. Redburn.

title: US Treasuries Post Third Week of Gains on Fed Rate-Cut Bets
content: US Treasuries closed out a third-straight positive week in a rally fueled by bets the Federal Reserve is ramping up to cut rates at least twice this year.

title: Lula to Go to Top Court to Challenge Overturn of Tax Decree
content: President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva’s administration will appeal to Brazil’s Supreme Court to try to preserve a tax decree that Congress overturned this week, according to two government officials familiar with the matter.

title: Platinum-Backed McGraw Hill Files for IPO Showing Narrowing Loss
content: Platinum Equity-backed McGraw Hill Inc. filed for an initial public offering, a sign that private equity firms are resurfacing to take more of their portfolio companies public.

title: Oil Steadies at End of Turbulent Week as Focus Shifts to Tariffs
content: Oil held steady as traders weighed the uncertain status of nuclear talks between the US and Iran against reports that OPEC+ may extend its run of super-sized production increases.

title: Bruckheimer Pushes Egos Aside to Get 'F1' in Theaters
content: "F1: The Movie" is now in theaters with a star studded cast including Brad Pitt, Damson Idris and Kerry Condon. Produced by seven-time Academy Award winner Jerry Bruckheimer, it is looking to give the summer box office season a speedy start. Bruckheimer sat down with Bloomberg Hot Pursuit Co-Hosts Matt Miller and Hannah Elliott ahead of its release. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: The Future of Venture Capital Investing: Uncharted Summit
content: Michael Loeb, founder and CEO of Loeb Enterprises and host of the Uncharted summit, talks about where he sees the future of venture capital investing and gives his thoughts on how artificial intelligence is shaking up business. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Labour’s ‘Starmtroopers’ Mount Rebellion Against Their Leader
content: Keir Starmer’s landslide UK general election win last July delivered to the House of Commons what was supposed to be a hand-picked army of loyalists molded in his image, a cadre that earned the moniker “Starmtroopers.” As the prime minister’s first anniversary in power approaches next week, the troops have mutinied, and some now have him and his chancellor in their sights.

content: Thai protesters began to rally in Bangkok on Saturday to demand the resignation of Prime Minister Paetongtarn Shinawatra, as the fallout continued from her controversial phone call with former Cambodian leader Hun Sen.

title: Canada’s Digital Services Tax Stays in Place Despite G-7 Deal

content: The US Supreme Court upheld a Texas law that requires porn sites to verify user age, rejecting arguments that the measure violates the speech rights of adults by requiring them to submit identification online.

title: Apple, Google Told DeepSeek App Is Illegal in Germany
content: Apple Inc. and Google’s Android have been warned by a top German privacy regulator that the Chinese AI service DeepSeek, available on their app stores, constitutes illegal content because it exposes users’ data to Chinese authorities.

title: Supreme Court Upholds $8.6 Billion FCC Telecom Subsidy Fund
content: The US Supreme Court upheld the $8.6 billion Universal Service Fund, the annual slate of subsidies that helps cover the cost of telecom services for low-income people, rural residents, schools and libraries.

title: Argentine Fintech tapi Buys Mastercard Unit in Mexico Expansion
content: Argentine payments services startup tapi has acquired the bill payment and cash-handling operations of Mastercard’s Arcus in Mexico, part of a bid to double-down on Latin America’s second-largest economy.

title: Macquarie-Owned Fiber Provider Taps Debt Advisors Amid Cash Burn
content: UK broadband provider KCOM Group Limited and its lenders are gearing up for debt talks as the business owned by Macquarie burns through cash.

title: Alibaba Unveils Latest AI Service for Images in Push for Users
content: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. unveiled a new iteration of its artificial-intelligence technology that will make it easier for users to generate and modify images from texts and visuals, as the Chinese e-commerce giant continues its aggressive push into AI.

title: Worldline’s Woes Deepen as Belgium Opens Probe Into Payment Firm
content: Worldline SA has long claimed to have cleaned up its payments business. Now, regulators and investors are testing that narrative after fresh allegations it overlooked fraud among high-risk clients.

content: Masayoshi Son acknowledged the outlines of a succession plan at SoftBank Group Corp., addressing what may be investors’ single biggest concern regarding the long-term future of the Japanese company.

content: Babbel’s new chief executive officer said he’s focused on expanding the company’s language-learning product to include emerging artificial intelligence tools, and he doesn’t intend to revive its initial public offering.

content: The Canadian economy is on track for a modest decline this quarter, yet isn’t deteriorating as fast as some economists feared.

title: UK Budget Reversals Threaten Reeves as Well as Her Fiscal Rules
content: Labour’s costly climbdowns on big policy plans don’t just leave Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves with the dilemma of how to find the money to meet her budget rules. They’re also starting to raise questions about her own job security.

title: Turkey Set to Skip Minimum-Wage Hike in Boost for Investors
content: Turkey’s government plans to skip a mid-year increase in the minimum wage, according to people with knowledge of the matter, resisting political pressure to alleviate rising living costs.

title: India Posts Current Account Surplus as Trade Gap Narrows
content: India’s current account returned a better than expected surplus in the January-March quarter as trade deficit narrowed following the revision of gold import data.

title: Spanish Economy Minister Cuerpo Runs for Eurogroup President
content: Spanish Economy Minister Carlos Cuerpo is running to head the Eurogroup, saying global developments require new leadership of the gatherings of euro-zone finance ministers.

title: Warning Signs of Weak Job Creation in the US
content: I’m  Mark Niquette, a US economy reporter in Columbus. Today we’re looking at the US labor market. Send us feedback and tips to ecodaily@bloomberg.net. And if you aren’t yet signed up to receive this newsletter, you can do so  here.

title: Fed’s Kashkari Sees Two Rate Cuts This Year Amid Tariff Unknowns
content: Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis President Neel Kashkari said he sees two interest-rate cuts as likely this year — with the first potentially in September — but warned that tariffs could have a delayed impact on inflation and policymakers should remain flexible.

title: China’s Central Bank Says Economy Is on Positive Track But Challenges Persist
content: China’s economy is showing positive signs and confidence is building, but challenges such as insufficient domestic demand and deflationary pressure persist, according to the country’s central bank.

title: Thai Finance Minister Heads to US for Trade Talks Next Week
content: Thai Finance Minister Pichai Chunhavajira will visit the US next week for tariff negotiations in an attempt to clinch a trade deal ahead of Washington’s deadline on July 9.

title: Chile Central Bank Policymaker Sees Good Omens After Long Inflation Fight
content: Chile’s central bank sees a set of factors coming together that will help bring inflation back down to target early in 2026, board member Luis Felipe Cespedes said in an interview.

title: French, Spanish Prices Tick Up But Not Enough to Worry ECB
content: Inflation inched up in France and Spain but not enough to concern European Central Bank officials who are optimistic that their 2% target will be met sustainably this year.

title: Starmer’s Latest U-Turn Risks £3 Billion Hit and More Tax Rises
content: Keir Starmer backed down to a rebellion within his own Labour party over a planned £5 billion ($6.9 billion) cut to disability entitlements, in a costly U-Turn that dents his authority and leaves his chancellor struggling to avoid tax hikes.

title: Thai Central Bank Vows to Step In If Baht Moves Are Unhinged
content: Thailand’s central bank is ready to tackle excessive baht volatility by managing any moves “unhinged” from its fundamentals, a deputy governor said, amid calls from local businesses to temper the currency’s rally to help exports and tourism.

title: ECB May Need to Hold Rates Amid ‘Two-Sided’ Risks, Knot Tells FT
content: The European Central Bank may have to keep borrowing costs steady for the forseeable future as officials confront both upside and downside risks to consumer prices, Governing Council member Klaas Knot said.

title: Lee Starts Term With 64% Rating on South Korea Recovery Optimism
content: South Korea’s new President Lee Jae Myung started his presidency with a higher approval rating than recent predecessors, as hopes for an economic recovery rise after months of political turbulence.

title: Ireland’s Firms Brace for Economic Hit With Quiet Confidence
content: Hundreds of companies, 200,000 jobs, billions of euro in corporation tax revenue. Add it all up and Ireland’s reliance on US investment for its economic success is starkly clear.

title: Thai Rate Pause Is Lifeline Saved for Turbulence Ahead, BOT Says
content: The Bank of Thailand’s decision to leave borrowing costs unchanged this week gives it a “monetary lifeline” to deal with challenges ranging from US tariffs and geopolitical tensions to domestic politics, according to Deputy Governor Piti Disyatat.

title: Lenders Find a Fast-Growing Market in Foreign Grad Students
content: Some startups take a broader view of grads’ ability to repay, looking to job prospects as support for lending.

title: Trump Officials Met With Walmart on Direct-to-Patient Drug Sales
content: US health officials met with with Walmart Inc., Amazon.com Inc. and other retailers this week as part of an effort to help Americans get their medicines more directly from companies that make them, according to people familiar with the talks.

title: GE Vernova Is Exploring a Sale of Its Proficy Software Business
content: GE Vernova Inc. is exploring a potential sale of its industrial software business known as Proficy, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Saks Gets $600 Million Lifeline as Creditors Face Steep Losses
content: Saks Global Enterprises has reached a $600 million debt deal with a number of its existing lenders that would force some creditors to accept losses and push them back in the repayment priority line.

title: Boeing Wins Buy Rating as Redburn Sees ‘Healthier’ Company
content: Shares of Boeing Co. are set to make gains as the company speeds up production of commercial aircraft and takes steps to move on from a series of crises in recent years, according to Rothschild & Co. Redburn.

title: Elon Musk Says First Tesla Drove Itself From Factory to Customer
content: Tesla Inc. Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk said a Tesla Model Y SUV drove itself from the company’s factory near Austin to a customer’s home in the company’s latest move to showcase its push into autonomous driving.

title: American Air Working to Fix Issue Causing Broad Flight Delays
content: American Airlines Group Inc. said it was working with its partners to resolve a “technology” issue that was causing flight delays on Friday.

title: Ford Forced to Idle Multiple US Plants on China Magnet Shortage
content: Ford Motor Co. temporarily idled factories in the US over the last three weeks due to a shortage of magnets containing rare earth minerals, key components embroiled in US trade tensions with China.

title: Caitlin Clark Ruled Out for Dallas WNBA Game With $3,000 Tickets
content: Caitlin Clark, the basketball star with the Indiana Fever, won’t play in Friday night’s game against the Dallas Wings, spoiling a matchup against the league’s top draft pick that spurred ballooning ticket prices.

title: California Democrats Push Reform to Stop Refinery Shutdowns
content: A group of California Democrats is looking to ease the state’s gasoline standards and streamline permitting for refineries in a bid to prevent more fuelmakers from shutting down and raising costs for the state’s drivers.

title: Keralty Blasts Petro After Top Colombia Court Sides With Insurer
content: Health group Keralty SAS said it will press ahead with legal action against the Colombian government after a top court overturned the takeover of its insurer in the South American nation.

title: Qatar Withdraws Interest for Rosneft’s German Operations
content: Qatar withdrew its interest in the seized German operations of Russia’s state-controlled oil company Rosneft PJSC, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Adler Weighs Sale of Prized €3.5 Billion Berlin Rental Portfolio
content: Adler Group SA is weighing the sale of its prized portfolio of Berlin apartments, a deal that would mark a landmark step in the slow unraveling of the scandal-hit German landlord.

title: Miami Brickell City Centre Shopping Mall Sells for $512 Million
content: Simon Property Group Inc. bought the retail and parking segments of Miami’s Brickell City Centre for roughly $512 million.

title: JPMorgan Shares Hit a Record This Week, But Baird Analysts Say Time to Sell
content: JPMorgan Chase & Co. shares have climbed nearly 40% from an April low and set record highs this week on a grab bag of positive developments, but to Baird analysts that’s too far, too fast.

title: Nike Surges After Predicting Its Sales Slump Has Hit Bottom
content: Nike Inc. said its yearlong sales decline is starting to ease, suggesting that Chief Executive Officer Elliott Hill’s strategic moves are paying off.

title: Gabon Signs $3.8 Billion Funding Pact With Afreximbank
content: Gabon signed a $3.8 billion memorandum of understanding with the African Export-Import Bank to fund mineral and infrastructure projects in the central African nation.

title: Federer Becomes a Tennis Billionaire: Business of Sports
content: The tennis great joins Michael Jordan and LeBron James as one of the few athletes to reach billionaire status.

title: Executives Get Combined 141 Years in Prison for Italy PFAS Spill
content: Eleven former executives of companies linked to Miteni SpA were sentenced to a combined 141 years in prison by an Italian court for one of the largest groundwater contaminations of forever chemicals in Europe.

title: Dangote Plans to List Africa’s Biggest Oil Refinery by Next Year
content: Aliko Dangote, Africa’s richest person, plans a stock listing for his Nigerian crude oil refinery by the end of next year to widen the company’s investor base.

title: Santander, Barclays Said to Be Final Bidders for Sabadell’s TSB
content: Banco Santander SA and Barclays Plc are the main contenders left in the race to acquire Banco Sabadell SA’s UK unit TSB, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Germany Considers Tighter Investment Rules Amid Nord Stream 2 Rumors
content: The German government is examining measures that could help it stop a potential sale of the Nord Stream 2 pipeline after speculation emerged earlier this year over reviving pipeline gas deliveries from Russia.

title: B. Riley Sells Financial Adviser to Private Equity Firm TorQuest
content: B. Riley Financial Inc. has sold its financial advisory services business GlassRatner to Canadian private equity firm TorQuest Partners, adding to a series of asset sales as the financial services firm deals with its woes.

title: Roger Federer's Long-Term Deals Make Him a Tennis Billionaire
content: Former star has net worth of about $1.3 billion, according to Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

title: UK Weighs Easing Impact of Trading Book Capital Rules on Banks
content: The Bank of England is considering ways to dilute the initial impact of new trading book capital rules so the UK can move forward with a wider package of global banking reforms even as the US drags its feet.

title: BBVA Favors Proceeding With Sabadell Bid If Investors Agree
content: BBVA SA is leaning toward proceeding with its takeover offer for Banco Sabadell SA and is sounding out investors to see if they still back the deal, after Spain said the lenders wouldn’t be allowed to fully merge for several years.

title: Tina Brown: ‘I’m Concerned About American Women’
content: The onetime Vanity Fair editor and Substack convert talks to Mishal Husain about the current moment in US politics, and what’s next for media.

title: Toyota Sales Hit Third Monthly Record on Japan, US Demand
content: Toyota Motor Corp.’s sales reached a third straight monthly record in May on strong demand for hybrid vehicles in the US, Japan and China, even as global automakers braced for big losses triggered by President Donald Trump’s tariffs on imported cars.

title: HSBC Asia Chairman’s Son Buys Hong Kong Homes for $29 Million
content: The son of an HSBC Holdings Plc leader has spent at least HK$231 million ($29 million) buying luxury properties in Hong Kong this year, as the city’s home prices hover at an eight-year low.

title: Mexico Steps In to Run Banks Tarred by US Drug Accusations
content: Mexico’s bank regulator stepped in to temporarily run three financial firms on Thursday, an extraordinary measure aimed at protecting customers following money-laundering accusations by US authorities the day before.
